question: In Greece, the universal postal service provider, Hellenic Post S.A., is closing more than 200 branches, including many in remote, mountainous and island regions. This development leaves entire areas - such as the Municipality of Zagori in Epirus with 43 villages or the Municipalities of Ierapetra in Crete, North Tzoumerka and Thermo in Aetolia-Acarnania without access to a local post office.

Similar cases are also being recorded in other regions. The shrinking of the network raises serious questions regarding compliance with the universal service obligation, which is a fundamental principle of European postal policy and requires equal access for all citizens, regardless of place of residence, to basic postal services.

In particular, for the elderly and vulnerable groups in rural areas the removal of service points entails exclusion from basic transactions, financial services and social communication. Accordingly: 1.

How does the Commission ensure that Greece complies with its universal postal service obligations, particularly in remote and island areas, in view of the closure of a large number of Hellenic Post branches?
What measures does the Commission intend to put in place to prevent the social and geographical exclusion of citizens due to the lack of access to basic postal services?

Is there a European strategy or financial instruments that can support the maintenance and/or modernisation of the presence of the universal postal service provider in areas with low population density?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.12.2025) The Postal Services Directive1 requires Member States to ensure that users enjoy the right to a permanent provision of a postal universal service at all points of the territory. However, the Directive does not specify the exact number or location of branches, the determination of which is a national competence.

The Greek national postal regulatory authority has informed the Commission that Hellenic Post has postponed closures in all non-urban areas and that discussions with Hellenic Post are underway. The Commission has announced in the Single Market Strategy2 that the regulatory framework for postal services including the Directive will be revised and a new EU Delivery Act is envisaged for the second half of 20263.

A call for evidence4 closed on 14 November 2025 and a public consultation will be launched in mid-December 2025 to enable stakeholders to provide feedback on the future regulatory framework including issues to which the Honorable Member refers to in his question.

Under the principle of shared management running Cohesion Policy funds, the project selection and implementation fall under the mere responsibility of the Member States. It should be noted that maintenance costs cannot be financed.
